claim_boundary: This evidence advances the repository-local G2 control-plane and qualification-preparation tranche. It demonstrates pure or read-only contracts for non-destructive installer planning, exact install-time model-profile selection, A/B trial-boot state, a typed privileged-helper boundary, bounded SQLite-backed request/effect ledgers, signed model-catalog verification, root-signed trust-bundle and exact anchored catalog admission, integrity-protected durable Admin authorization events, inert offline installation-source descriptors with repeated schema-v3 raw-byte revalidation, and Ubuntu host admission/inventory. It also provides operator approval and physical-qualification procedures. It does not demonstrate a bootable OS, disk mutation, an actual signed production catalog or protected key ceremony, a production authenticated Admin writer or protected external anchor, artifact-byte consumption, Secure Boot/UKI/dm-verity/LUKS2 behavior, enforcing cgroup/AppArmor/seccomp/KVM/device/peer controls, recovery, power-loss behavior, or either physical A1 board.

items.subject: non-destructive-installer-preflight-and-destructive-confirmation-contract
items.observations: Fifteen deterministic tests cover exact hardware/disk identity, same-device accelerator qualification, capacity, issued-plan provenance, release/payload/policy binding, authenticated confirmation, effect-time authority, expiry, fresh revalidation, opaque locked-device capabilities, and a durable in-doubt/completed attempt-journal contract. The executor is injected and no disk or OS tool is invoked.
items.limitations: The real binder must exclusively open, lock, re-identify, and retain the exact raw-device handle; the real journal must provide crash-safe durability. Destructive installation and encryption recovery remain blocked.

items.subject: authenticated-ab-trial-boot-and-fallback-contract
items.observations: Thirteen deterministic tests cover distinct physical slot identities, authenticated state, an external monotonic anchor, hash-linked operation records, monotonic fence epochs, anti-downgrade sequencing, attested boot attempts, essential-health binding, tamper evidence, checkpoint durability/readability, and power-loss reconciliation. Production runtime assertions are prohibited and the suite passes under optimized Python.
items.limitations: Authenticator, anchor CAS, boot observation, durability/readback, bootloader, UKI, verity, encryption, and physical power-loss adapters are injected or absent; no physical boot occurred.

items.subject: typed-privileged-helper-and-confinement-contract
items.observations: Twenty-four deterministic tests cover closed typed actions, canonical bounded input, authenticated peer revalidation immediately before dispatch, request-bound confinement attestations and authority, opaque stable-device capabilities, signed driver/runtime certificate binding, effect-time revocation, persistent pending/completed/failed-unknown journal reconciliation, executor idempotency, known-not-applied capacity exhaustion, reentrant-callback denial, and integration with the bounded SQLite request journal and idempotent effect ledger. The suite passes under optimized Python.
items.limitations: The real service must obtain kernel peer credentials, verify signatures and OS enforcement, safely bind devices, provide an atomic durable journal, and operate under bounded watchdogs. No privileged action is executed by this module.

items.subject: cross-platform-repository-validation
items.observations: The referenced detached sidecars record the prior integrated repository run on native Windows and Ubuntu WSL. Focused current-tranche suites have been exercised separately, but a new full-run and reproducible-archive sidecar must be produced only after the integration commit. Both development lanes remain guests of one physical laptop.
items.limitations: Repository tests validate contracts and regressions only. The dated test-run and archive-attestation paths are immutable detached repository sidecars intentionally excluded from release archives; they do not attest the current uncommitted tranche. These results do not satisfy any physical-board, destructive-media, boot, encryption, confinement, performance, or lifecycle acceptance procedure.

items.subject: durable-sqlite-request-and-effect-ledger-integration
items.observations: Nineteen deterministic durable-ledger tests exercise bounded authenticated SQLite request/effect records, writer fencing, idempotency, crash-window ambiguity, post-APPLYING current-state revalidation with safe PREPARED restoration, reconciliation, capacity limits, clock rollback, and corruption rejection. The privileged-helper suite integrates the same SQLite request journal and idempotent effect executor across completed, prepared, applying, and known-not-applied capacity recovery paths.
items.limitations: The SQLite ledgers were exercised with development files on one laptop. SQLite cannot make an external host mutation transactional; a production adapter, protected storage policy, watchdog, and physical crash/power-loss reconciliation evidence remain required.

items.subject: model-pack-v2-install-time-profile-selection-and-binding-contract
items.observations: Twenty dedicated model-pack/model-selection tests and five installer-integration tests cover schema-v2 exact total/active counts through 405B, ordered shards and capabilities, explicit manual-only/CPU/CUDA profiles, JSON-safe resource arithmetic, exact pack/runtime/context/resource binding, single-device CUDA fit, denial without substitution, verified-pack bridging, and effect-time catalog/hardware revalidation.
items.limitations: The exercised Qwen3-4B artifact and derived tuple are unsigned development inputs. No signed production catalog, base-image integration, destructive installation, native Ubuntu board, two-board run, complete offline workflow, pressure/recovery qualification, or certified 400–405B hardware result exists.

items.subject: signed-model-catalog-verification-and-custody-contract
items.observations: Twelve deterministic tests pass on native Windows and Ubuntu WSL under normal and optimized Python. They cover a canonical request-before-approval ceremony, three distinct production approval events plus a separate signing custodian, exact release/catalog/sequence/policy/validity/key/assignment binding, purpose and environment separation, signing-time and current authorization/key lifecycle checks, same-sequence digest rollback protection, exact pack/runtime/certification binding, bounded untrusted inputs, tamper rejection, and digest-bound verification receipts. The ceremony utility never accepts a private key.
items.limitations: Repository-local anchored trust/catalog and durable Admin development adapters now exist, but no production root provisioning, protected HSM provider, authenticated Admin writer service, per-deployment rollback anchor/secret custody, signed model pack/certificates, protected key material, or completed human ceremony exists. These contracts cannot make an unsigned development catalog production-eligible.

items.subject: read-only-ubuntu-host-inventory-and-native-candidate-admission
items.observations: Twenty deterministic tests pass on native Windows and Ubuntu WSL, and a live read-only WSL collector-to-preflight run reports Ubuntu 26.04 WSL2 with certification_closing=false. Native admission requires an explicit E1/E2 class, fresh complete inventory, live host/kernel/identity/security/firmware/accelerator corroboration, trusted absolute root-owned command provenance, and no disk reclassification or selection. WSL is structurally unable to pass native-candidate mode.
items.limitations: The observed WSL environment is Ubuntu 26.04 on the same physical Windows laptop, with a Windows-mounted checkout and no native UEFI/Secure Boot/AppArmor/TPM result. Inventory and preflight are admission evidence only; they do not authorize destruction or prove installation, boot, isolation, recovery, lifecycle, or hardware performance.

items.subject: operator-approval-and-physical-qualification-package
items.observations: The package specifies owner-provided E1/E2 hardware, exact disposable-disk authorization, firmware and recovery access, network isolation, production signing custody, model/license inputs, witnesses, stop rules, test oracles, evidence layout, and sign-off for the complete G2 physical, security, recovery, lifecycle, and performance scope.
items.limitations: A reviewed procedure is not execution evidence. No destructive installation, physical boot, tamper, LUKS2/TPM recovery, power interruption, enforcing isolation, suspend/resume, lifecycle, performance, or two-board workflow was run.

items.subject: root-signed-trust-and-anchored-catalog-admission
items.observations: Deterministic normal and optimized tests exercise root-authorized trust bundles, environment/purpose separation, effective validity containment, exact monotonic checkpoints, catalog admission plans committed by compare-and-swap, transitive live trust/catalog freshness, fail-closed clock and anchor outages, and a concrete public Ed25519 verification provider. An admitted catalog remains authoritative only while its exact catalog and trust checkpoints remain current.
items.limitations: Development in-memory anchors and test roots are not production rollback protection or custody. Production still requires provisioned offline roots, an independently protected monotonic anchor, trusted time and provider composition, HSM-backed signing operations, key lifecycle procedures, and witnessed recovery/revocation ceremonies.

items.subject: integrity-protected-durable-admin-authorization-event-log
items.observations: A dependency-free SQLite event log uses canonical bounded events, an externally held HMAC secret, hash chaining, monotonic sequence, exact schema-object checks, committed-head readback, restart verification, and an external digest-anchor checkpoint. Every append requires a mandatory external Admin writer authorizer. A complete catalog-authorization call performs one bounded fresh authenticated replay, verifies exact before/after database-head and anchor state, retains no long-lived authorization cache, and observes a durable revocation on the next call.
items.limitations: The HMAC protects stored integrity and does not authenticate the human or service writer. SQLite and the external anchor are not one transaction: DB-ahead or anchor-ahead states require typed fail-closed reconciliation. The current fixed log domain is development-only; production requires an authenticated isolated Admin service, trusted time, protected secret custody, and unique per-deployment/service domain and anchor namespace. Maximum-capacity replay, anchor latency, native filesystem behavior, and lock contention remain unqualified on target hardware.

items.subject: inert-offline-source-and-installer-schema-v3-revalidation
items.observations: Schema-v3 preflight validates immutable canonical descriptor bytes against a caller pin, contract-fixed environment, and exact live anchored catalog admission. Execution obtains and fully validates fresh raw source input before binding/journaling and again after journaling, then resamples model hardware, reselects the profile from that admission catalog, reauthorizes, checks catalog/trust currentness, and checks confirmation, inventory, and time freshness immediately before the injected executor.
items.limitations: The descriptor is inert and contains no catalog; the catalog is validation context recorded by digest-bound receipts. The caller pin is not governance, a cached validation result is never reusable authority, and no installer consumes or verifies release artifact bytes/signatures. Real offline media creation, governed release pins, exclusive device handling, signed artifact consumption, destructive install, boot, and recovery evidence remain absent.

closure_rule: G2 remains blocked until T01-T16, applicable T27-T30, T33, T40, T45-T51, and T62; the complete vertical workflow on both physical A1 boards; and all required signed-media, storage, recovery, confinement, security, lifecycle, failure, and performance evidence pass.
